casting-call: New-Machine Setup, End to End

Everything it takes to go from a fresh Mac to a working call-recording rig: install the tools, wire the Zoom PodTrak P4next, record a screen call as four audio tracks (a master mix, you, the far side, and a marker track) with the P4next's card as a backup, and turn it into a transcript with your flagged moments dropped in at the right spot. Follow it top to bottom the first time.

Sections are tagged terminal when they are copy-paste commands (safe to hand to an agent) or in the app when they are clicks in OBS or on the P4next that only a human can do. The flow the whole thing produces is in docs/pipeline-flow.html if you want the picture first.

What you end up with

The P4next is the Mac's audio interface. Your mic plugs into it, Meet uses it as mic and speaker, and it feeds OBS every channel separately over USB. OBS records your screen plus four audio tracks into one .mkv: Track 1 is the master mix, Track 2 is your mic, Track 3 is computer audio (Meet, Slack, Zoom, everything the Mac plays), and Track 4 is silent except where you pressed pad A, which plays a short clip that says "marker". At the same time the P4next writes every channel to its own microSD card with no Mac software in the path.

After the call, one command splits the tracks, transcribes them, cleans up the junk Whisper invents on silence, and folds your presses in as [MARKER] marker lines with a full-resolution screen grab each. If an OBS track dropped, it fills the gap from the card take. If there is no card take, the Meet captions on screen are the backup.

Part 1: The command line terminal

This whole part is safe to run start to finish. It installs the tools, pulls the repo, and regenerates the marker clip locally (the .wav files are gitignored, so they do not come down with the clone).

# Homebrew, if this machine does not have it yet
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

# Tools: ffmpeg + whisper for audio, tesseract for the caption fallback, OBS
brew install ffmpeg whisper-cpp tesseract
brew install --cask obs

# Python deps (Homebrew's python3; --break-system-packages is required on it)
pip3 install --break-system-packages pillow numpy pytesseract pytest

# Whisper model, ~3 GB, one time
mkdir -p ~/whisper-models
curl -o ~/whisper-models/ggml-large-v3.bin -L \
  'https://huggingface.co/ggerganov/whisper.cpp/resolve/main/ggml-large-v3.bin?download=true'

# Silero VAD model (~1 MB, one time) so Whisper only transcribes real speech and
# stops inventing looped lines on non-speech audio
curl -sL -o ~/whisper-models/ggml-silero-v5.1.2.bin \
  https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/whisper-vad/resolve/main/ggml-silero-v5.1.2.bin

# The repo
git clone https://github.com/samgutentag/casting-call.git ~/Developer/casting-call
cd ~/Developer/casting-call

# Your roster (real names stay local; this file is gitignored)
cp speakers_roster.example.json speakers_roster.json
# then edit speakers_roster.json: set "self" to your name, list the people you call

# The marker clip (regenerated here; not committed). One clip, one word.
# The P4next sound pads only accept 44.1 or 48 kHz WAV, so it is 48 kHz,
# 24-bit stereo. ripa finds presses by silence detection, so the word itself
# is for your ears when you scrub the audio, not for Whisper.
mkdir -p obs/marker-clips
say -o /tmp/_m.aiff "marker"
ffmpeg -loglevel error -i /tmp/_m.aiff -ar 48000 -ac 2 -c:a pcm_s24le \
  -af "apad=pad_dur=0.25" obs/marker-clips/MARKER.WAV -y
rm -f /tmp/_m.aiff

# Short names for the three commands you run after every call
cat >> ~/.zshrc <<'ALIASES'
alias ripcard="bash ~/Developer/casting-call/bin/pull_card.sh"
alias ripa="bash ~/Developer/casting-call/bin/extract_audio_stereo.sh"
alias ripv="bash ~/Developer/casting-call/bin/convert_video.sh"
ALIASES

# Confirm the toolchain is sane
python3 -m pytest -q

If the tests pass, the software side is done. The clip now lives at ~/Developer/casting-call/obs/marker-clips/MARKER.WAV, which goes onto P4next pad A in Part 3.

If python3 offers to install "command line developer tools," let it, then rerun the last two commands. The scripts and Whisper only need what you just installed.

Part 2: The P4next in the app

  1. Plug the RØDE PodMic into INPUT 1, your headphones into the P4next, and the P4next into the Mac over USB. Put a microSD card in it and leave it there.
  2. In the P4next Menu, set:
    SettingValue
    Recording file typeMulti Track
    USB Audio Interface ModeMulti Track
    Mix MinusOn
    Play Key in RecMark Only
  3. On the Mac, set both System Settings, Sound input and output to ZOOM P4next. In Meet, pick ZOOM P4next as mic and speaker. Meet uses USB channel 1, your mic.

Over USB the P4next hands the Mac these channels. Channels 11 and 12 leave out the computer audio because Mix Minus is On, so OBS builds the master mix on Track 1 itself.

P4next USB channelCarries
1your mic (INPUT 1)
7 and 8computer audio (every app the Mac plays)
9 and 10sound pads
11 and 12P4next master (not used)
Mute in Meet, never with MUTE 1 on the P4next. Meet's mute stops the far side hearing you, but your muted notes still land on the card and on OBS Track 2, which is how "action item" and "notes notes notes" said into a muted mic reach the transcript. MUTE 1 silences the mic everywhere, card included.

Part 3: The marker pad in the app

  1. On the P4next, open Menu, USB File Transfer so the card mounts on the Mac as /Volumes/P4NEXT_SD (the same mode ripcard uses after every call). Copy obs/marker-clips/MARKER.WAV into the card's P4next_SoundPad folder, then eject and leave USB File Transfer.
  2. Menu, Sound Pad, A, Sound Assign: pick MARKER.WAV. Play Mode: One-Shot.

Pad A plays on USB channels 9 and 10, which only OBS Track 4 records (Part 4). Mix Minus keeps it out of what Meet hears, so the far side never hears a press. It does land in the card's stereo mix, which is what you want when you scrub the watch video later.

Part 4: OBS, recording four tracks in the app

OBS records MKV on purpose. If a recording ever crashes, an MKV is still readable where an MP4 would be corrupt. You never remux it; the pipeline reads the MKV directly.

  1. Open OBS. Skip or click through the auto-config wizard.
  2. Settings, Output. Set Output Mode to Advanced. On the Recording tab set Recording Format to Matroska Video (.mkv), and under Audio Track check 1, 2, 3, and 4.
  3. Settings, Audio. Set every Global Audio Device (Desktop Audio and Mic/Auxiliary Audio) to Disabled. Left on, they record the P4next a second time onto every track.
  4. Create a scene named Call P4 and add these sources to it:
    1. Display Capture (or Window Capture) for the screen. This is the video. Leave its audio off.
    2. Three Audio Input Capture sources, each on device ZOOM P4next, with the channels below picked for left and right:
      Source nameChannels (left / right)Tracks
      P4 MicCh 1 / Ch 11 and 2
      P4 ComputerCh 7 / Ch 81 and 3
      P4 MarkerCh 9 / Ch 104 only
  5. Assign tracks. Click the gear in the Audio Mixer, choose Advanced Audio Properties. For each of the three P4 rows, check exactly the Tracks in the table above and set Audio Monitoring to Monitor Off. You already hear everything live through the P4next's headphone out, so OBS monitoring would only add a delayed second copy in your ears. P4 Marker must never touch Tracks 1, 2 or 3, or Whisper transcribes the clip as speech.
The one setting that will silently eat your markers: the recording output has to record Track 4, and P4 Marker has to feed it. If either is off, the pad plays and none of it ends up where the pipeline looks. ripa warns when the marker track is digital silence, and with a card take it reads the presses from the card's pad file instead. Sanity check a test recording with ffprobe recording.mkv and count four audio streams.

Part 5: Prove it works before a real call terminal + in the app

  1. Start recording in OBS and press REC on the P4next, then press pad A once. Talk for a few seconds, play a few seconds of any video on the Mac, press pad A again, and stop both.
  2. Move the .mkv into a folder, say ~/calls/test/. On the P4next open Menu, USB File Transfer, run ripcard, and leave File Transfer as soon as it prints Card ejected. Exit USB File Transfer on the P4next now. The take is now in ~/Desktop/P4next-takes/<take>/. Move that take folder into ~/calls/test/ next to the .mkv.
  3. Confirm the file really has four audio tracks: 
    ffprobe -v error -show_entries stream=index,codec_type -of csv ~/calls/test/*.mkv
# expect one 'video' line and four 'audio' lines
  4. Run the pipeline and read the result: 
    cd ~/Developer/casting-call
bash bin/extract_audio_stereo.sh ~/calls/test
cat ~/calls/test/*/*.txt
    You should see [You] and [Caller] lines, two [MARKER] marker lines where you pressed pad A, a PNG for each in <name>/markers/, and a header line saying the card lined up by the marker method.

If both presses come back, the card lines up, and nobody on the far side heard the pad, the rig is done.

Part 6: The daily loop

  1. Start recording in OBS and on the P4next, then press pad A once right away. That first press is what lines the card up with the video to the millisecond. Press it again during the call whenever something matters.
  2. Stop both recorders. Drop the .mkv in a folder.
  3. On the P4next open Menu, USB File Transfer and run ripcard. It copies every take not already pulled into ~/Desktop/P4next-takes/<take>/ (CARD_INBOX moves it), ejects the card, and prints Card ejected. Exit USB File Transfer on the P4next now. Do that right away: while File Transfer is on, the P4next is not the Mac's audio device and you hear nothing from the computer. Nothing on the card is ever deleted or changed, and the unused MIC2 to MIC4 files stay on the card (PULL_ALL_INPUTS=1 copies them too).
  4. Move the recordings that matter into their day folder, ~/Desktop/call_logs/<yyyy-wNN>/<yyyy-mm-dd>/, and rename each .mkv to something you will recognize, say 2026-11-10-corey-sync.mkv. Move its take folder out of ~/Desktop/P4next-takes/ into the same day folder and rename it to match: 2026-11-10-corey-sync.card/. Leave the files inside with their P4next names. A take folder you forget to rename still works: ripa pairs an unrenamed yymmdd_hhmmss/ folder with the recording that started closest to it, says how far apart the two starts were, and refuses past 10 minutes. Use mv (or a Finder move on the same disk) for the .mkv, which keeps the creation time that pairing reads.
  5. ripa <day folder>, whenever you like. It reads each take where it sits and never moves it, and never reads the card or the P4next-takes inbox, which is only a staging area. That is the transcript, markers and all, ready to hand to an LLM, plus a health line per track saying whether OBS dropped anything and whether the card covered it.
  6. Optional, only when you want to watch it back: ripv <folder> renders a playable .mp4. With a card take its soundtrack is the card's stereo mix, lined up to the video; without one it is OBS Track 1. An .mp4 rendered before ripa lined the card up is rendered again.
  7. Optional, to put real names on the far-side lines: bash bin/extract_speakers.sh <recording> --region x,y,w,h --transcript <transcript>.
Older recordings still work. Files from the Elgato Wave and Stream Deck rig, with seven marker clips on Track 4, are read the same way they always were: ripa listens to the first few presses and switches to the seven-clip parser when it hears one of the old phrases. MARKER_MODE=legacy forces it.

Part 7: When an OBS track drops out

OBS audio capture can die mid-call and record silence from that point on, with no error in its log. The lines Whisper would have invented on that dead audio are stripped automatically, so the transcript does not fill up with fake "thank you" and "subtitles by" junk.

With a card take, the gap is filled from the card. ripa lines the card up with the video (pad presses first, then speech, then the two clocks), and any stretch where OBS Track 2 or Track 3 is silent while the card's MIC1 or USB file has sound is cut from the card and spliced in before transcription. The transcript header names which spans came from the card and how it was lined up.

Without a card take, for Google Meet calls, any stretch of a minute or more where Track 3 is quiet gets the Meet captions read over just that stretch. If they show someone other than you talking, the capture dropped, and their caption lines are spliced into the transcript as [Caller] lines. The transcript from before the splice is kept as parts/pre-caption-splice.txt and the raw caption lines as parts/captions.txt. If the captions show only you, the quiet was real and nothing changes.

It finds the captions by Meet's red end-call button, which always sits right under them, so you can move and resize the Meet window during the call. What it needs: captions turned on, and the Meet window on screen for the stretch that dropped. Frames where Meet is hidden are skipped. Caption speaker names are approximate when people talk over each other, which is fine for lines that are labeled [Caller] anyway. CAPTION_BACKUP=0 ripa ... turns the check off.

Calls in Zoom, Slack or Roam are not covered: ripa still drops the junk and the transcript has a gap. To rebuild a whole recording from a fixed caption region by hand:

bash bin/stitch_captions.sh <recording> --region x,y,w,h
